title: OKR Alignment Gateway and Quarterly Handshake Protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we scale Redwood’s product and org teams, company-level OKRs are drifting from engineering and design roadmaps. There is inconsistent interpretation of initiative boundaries, and frequent last-minute reprioritizations that ripple into Dedicated/Private product work and customer SLAs.

Goal: Define and operationalize a lightweight 'Alignment Gateway' — a quarterly handshake protocol and set of artifacts (signal definitions, gating metrics, owner contracts, and a decision runbook) to ensure cross-functional commitment discipline. The Gateway should reduce cross-team rework by 30% for company initiatives and provide a repeatable cadence for rolling up team OKRs into company objectives.

Scope: Company-level OKR intake, initiative scoping, cross-functional owner assignments, gating metrics (health, cost, latency, privacy), timing windows (handshake, commit, execution), and a lightweight escalation path into the leadership triage. Workstream includes templates, Console dashboards, Linear automation for commitment windows, and a roll-forward play for downstream Dedicated/Private customers impacted by scope changes.

Out of scope: Deep engineering delivery planning (sprint-level), per-team backlog grooming. This ticket focuses on the alignment layer, tooling hooks (links to dashboards/PRs), and governance process.
acceptance_criteria: Alignment Gateway template published in Confluence with step-by-step handshake checklist and owner contract
Quarterly handshake runbook validated with at least 4 cross-functional stakeholders (Eng, Design, Security, Revenue) and signed off
Linear automation: a template issue type created that enforces 'handshake complete' flag before initiative moves from Planned -> In Progress
Console dashboard shows company-level initiative health (OKR progress, latency SLO delta, estimated cost delta) for pilot initiatives
Two pilot initiatives complete full gateway cycle with measurable reduction in post-commit scope churn (target: >= 30% reduction)
comments: 2026-02-16 / AP: Kickoff meeting notes — stakeholders: Liam (PM), Priya (Eng), Mateo (Design), Hana (Security), Jordan (Revenue). Agreed success metrics and pilot candidates (initiative A: KV-cache improvements; initiative B: Dedicated autoscaling policy).

2026-02-20 / LO: Drafted handshake checklist and owner-contract template. Raised trade-off: too many gating metrics will slow teams; propose 3 mandatory gates (health, cost delta, privacy impact) + up to 2 optional per-project metrics.
2026-02-24 / Priya R (Eng): Raised implementation constraint for Linear automation — we can add issue-state guards but need 1 week to QA the Linear webhook. Blocker flagged until 2026-03-02.
2026-03-01 / Design review: Mateo uploaded mockups for the Console initiative health panel (link below). Feedback: make cost delta visualization per-token and per-route, not per-model aggregate.

2026-03-03 / LO: Incorporated feedback and updated Confluence draft. Added escalation path to leadership triage with SLAs: 48h triage response for high-impact blockers, 5-day resolution window for scope decisions affecting Dedicated customers.
2026-03-05 / AP: Executive review scheduled 2026-03-10. Need rubric for when to apply 'federated' vs 'centralized' ownership for cross-team initiatives. Action: LO to prepare short decision matrix.
risks: If we centralize too many decisions at the company layer, team autonomy and velocity may suffer. Conversely, a purely federated model will keep the same drift we see today. There is an engineering cost (Linear automation + Console panels) and a people cost (weekly handshake meetings).
decision_log: 02/20: Adopted minimum gates (health/cost/privacy). 03/03: Escalation SLAs approved by Head of Product. 03/05: Prepare decision matrix for centralized vs federated ownership and present to execs.
next_steps: 1) Finish Linear webhook QA (ENG) by 2026-03-09. 2) Finalize Confluence templates and owner-contract by 2026-03-08. 3) Exec review on 2026-03-10. 4) Run two pilots during Q2 2026 and measure churn reduction.
notes: Pilot initiative selection prioritized projects with clear customer SLAs and measurable cost/latency metrics. Security review flagged because Dedicated/Private changes can carry compliance implications; Hana (Security) assigned as reviewer.
